positions.name: KestrelwoodRecordErasure
positions.frame: what should the record retain about the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration history, and does any prior observatory event support it?
positions.why: The two erasure directives (src-1, src-2) share a single imperative move — discard everything tied to the Kestrelwood spectrograph, its 88.4 MHz figure, and Quill Ashgrove's calibration work — and the closing assertive (src-3) supplies the factual predicate that licenses the erasure by denying the underlying event ever occurred. Read together they enact one revisionist stance toward the record, even though the directional passes register a conviction gradient across the set: src-1/src-2 sit at decision-level performed acts ('Forget', 'Remove all knowledge') while src-3 lands as a flatter claim-level assertion ('never calibrated it'). That shift in register is held as tension within the frame rather than resolved — the group is bound by shared subject and shared erasure-direction, not by uniform delivery.
